subject: literature
passage: When his sons offered to buy him an outboard motor, old Tomás thanked them and went on rowing. They argued that the motor would get him to the fishing grounds in a quarter of the time, and he agreed that it would. But he had rowed the same stretch of bay for fifty years, and he knew the water by the pull of it against the oars: where the current quickened over the sandbar, where the cold spring welled up from the bottom. A motor would have ______ him from all of that. The time saved, he said, was time he did not want.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Tomás knows the bay "by the pull of it against the oars." A motor would mean no more rowing, so he would lose that direct contact with the water. The blank needs a word meaning "cut off," and "separated ... from" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The motor would not divert his attention from the water; it would remove the contact through which he feels it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Freed from" suggests escaping a burden, but Tomás does not want to escape the water; he turns the motor down to keep that contact.
explanation.C: Correct. Without the oars, Tomás would no longer feel the water, so a motor would separate him from the knowledge he prizes.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The currents and cold springs are not dangers Tomás wants protection from; they are things he values knowing.
